title: [Alerting v2] Drop no-op form interactions from the edit-mode submit test
body:
Fixes #269126

### Summary

- `ActionPolicyFormPage > edit mode > submits update payload on save` was timing out at **5.107s** against the default 5000ms Jest budget.
- It performed four click/tab interactions on the name and description inputs before clicking submit. They write no values and do not gate the submit button — each one just drives an `onBlur` validation cycle that re-renders the entire four-section `ActionPolicyForm`.
- This drops those four interactions so the test goes straight from `renderPage()` to clicking submit. The assertions are untouched.

| Runtime vs. 5s budget | Passed | Avg | Max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before fix | 25/25 | 593ms | 627ms |
| After fix | 25/25 | 186ms | 197ms |

### Context

- Follows the [failed-test investigator's proposed fix](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/269126#issuecomment-5814990817) exactly.
- The interactions are provably no-ops for this test: `isSubmitEnabled` is derived purely from watched form values, and `toFormState(EXISTING_POLICY)` already satisfies every clause on first render (non-empty name, one workflow destination, `per_field` with two `group_by` fields, a valid `5m` interval), so submit is enabled before the test touches anything. A click-then-tab on a text input writes no value, so the asserted payload is unchanged.
- This is a time-budget problem, not a waiting problem. [`asyncUtilTimeout` is 4500ms](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/main/src/platform/packages/shared/kbn-test/src/jest/setup/react_testing_library.js#L21), so once the test is this close to the ceiling the Jest timeout fires before `waitFor` can even report what it was waiting on — waiting differently would not have helped, only removing the work does.
- The `waitFor(() => expect(updateButton).toBeEnabled())` guard is deliberately kept; it settles on the first poll and costs nothing.
- Recurring on `kibana-on-merge` (`main` and `9.5`) since May 2026, most recently [build 110757](https://buildkite.com/elastic/kibana-on-merge/builds/110757#01a0d367-17ba-455e-b579-6e165222cc90) on 2026-09-24. The original `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` double-call signature has not reappeared since the file moved to `mutateAsync` with the assertion inside `waitFor`; every recurrence since [Jul 28](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/269126#issuecomment-5104310168) is the 5s timeout, so this is treated as a fresh flake at a different step rather than a prior fix failing.
- `action_policy_form_flyout.test.tsx` carries a copy of the same no-op block and timed out in the same job. It is left out of this PR to keep the change focused and to avoid colliding with a separate fixer run on its own issue.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

#### Verified locally

- ✅ Passed: `node scripts/eslint x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/alerting_v2/public/pages/action_policy_form_page/action_policy_form_page.test.tsx`
- ✅ Passed: `node scripts/jest x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/alerting_v2/public/pages/action_policy_form_page/action_policy_form_page.test.tsx` — 25/25 passed before the fix (avg 593ms, max 627ms), 25/25 after (avg 186ms, max 197ms). The whole 12-test file passes in both loops, confirming the dropped interactions were not load-bearing.

#### Not verified locally

- The flake does **not** reproduce on this runner: the unpatched test never exceeded 627ms, versus 5.107s on the CI agent. The clean pre-fix loop therefore proves nothing about flakiness — the meaningful signal is the **3.2× drop in average runtime**, which shows the patch removes real work rather than changing how the test waits. Scaling the CI figure by the same ratio puts the test at ≈1.6s against the 5s budget.
- Neither loop ran under CI's parallel load.
- No type check was run (left to CI).

</details>

> [!NOTE]
> Share feedback in #kibana-qa. Mention `@copilot` to make quick changes.
